steps.title: Find Your Local Bürgeramt
steps.description: Identify the Bürgeramt (citizens' office) responsible for your district. In most German cities, you can register at any Bürgeramt, but it is often faster to go to the one closest to your new address. Check your city's official website for the nearest office.

steps.title: Book an Appointment Online
steps.description: Most Bürgerämter require an appointment. Visit your city's online appointment portal to book a slot. In Berlin, use service.berlin.de. Appointments can fill up quickly, so book as early as possible — ideally before you arrive in Germany.

steps.title: Gather Required Documents
steps.description: Prepare all required documents before your appointment. The exact list depends on your situation (student, worker, etc.), but you will always need your passport, a completed registration form (Anmeldeformular), and a landlord confirmation (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung).

steps.title: Visit the Bürgeramt
steps.description: Arrive at the Bürgeramt on time with all your documents. The process usually takes 10–15 minutes. A clerk will review your documents and enter your information into the system. Basic German or English is usually sufficient, but bringing a German-speaking friend can help.

steps.title: Receive Your Anmeldebestätigung
steps.description: After successful registration, you will receive a registration confirmation (Anmeldebestätigung or Meldebescheinigung). This is an important official document — keep it safe. You will need it for opening a bank account, signing up for health insurance, and other administrative tasks.

steps.title: Update Your Records
steps.description: After registering, inform your university, employer, health insurance provider, and bank of your registered address. If you move to a new address within Germany, you must complete a new Anmeldung within 14 days of moving in.
